To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new framework for analyzing general NVAR processes, called independent innovation analysis, that guarantees the identifiabilty of the innovations, and we propose two practical estimation algorithms for the method.

we propose a general NVAR model that can be used for analysis of general nonlinear dynamics, we prove its identifiability under the assumption of mutual independence of the errors and a fully observable auxiliary time variable, and we provide practical methods for estimating the model parameters from data.

we propose a general framework called independent innovations analysis (IIA) for learning nonlinear vector autoregressions (NVAR) and that IIA guarantees identifiability of NVAR with arbitrary nonlinearities up to a permutation of variables and component-wise invertibility of nonlinearities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given an observed multivariate time series, how to estimate the innovations that drive the underlying nonlinear dynamics?
a generalization of the VAR model, which is one of the most fundamental models in time series analysis.
the problem of learning nonlinear dynamical systems from multivariate time series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed IIA framework is able to provide a rigorous identifiability guarantee for general nonlinear vector autoregressions.
we provide the first rigorous analysis of general NVARS, which is a long-standing problem in nonlinear time series analysis.
IIA can be used to learn any NVAR model with arbitrary nonlinearities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework to estimate the innovations from general NVAR, and the framework can be easily implemented.
we provide a new framework for learning the innovations of general NVAR.

we have developed a new general framework for analyzing multivariate nonlinear time series, which is based on the assumption that innovations are independent of the past, and can be modulated by an observable auxiliary variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the innovations can be estimated from general nonlinear dynamical systems, even if they are highly nonlinearly dependent.
the innovations of a general NVAR are identifiable, even if they are nonlinearly coupled, provided they are mutually independent.
the NVAR model can be extended to the most general setting without losing the ability to identify its innovation, which is a fundamental building block in many applications.
